title: When Evaluation Pipelines Change the Task
subtitle: Source-grounded audits of task kind, requests and scoring references

blocks.text: Private working manuscript | 14 November 2026 | Evidence synthesis v1.6
Abstract

Evaluation software can change task kind, remove required information and alter scoring references while returning numeric scores. We audit a pinned One-Eval revision using official records, native methods, controlled interventions and an existing two-model trial. A prospective four-contract extension found malformed ARC-Challenge and OpenBookQA construction, followed by captured-split confirmation. In a 50-question WinoGrande panel, Qwen's source-correct gain under joint question and format repair remains between 36 and 48 percentage points under conservative unknown-answer treatment. Re-scoring identical repaired-prompt outputs changes assigned scores by 40 and 42 points for the two models. Causal ablations isolate shared source-symbol and option-decoding faults, followed by a confirmed prediction on 100 French MMMLU records. MixEval reveals a distinct task-kind mismatch despite field presence and internally consistent inferred settings. Source placeholders are displayed as answer choices. Controlled scorer replays on 200 reused records reject all original list references yet return numeric zero. A separate fixed-output study matches 49 public responses and confirms reference exclusion; typed optional official rule scoring preserves interpretable outcomes and its own counterexamples. These replays isolate scorer behavior. A subsequent 20-question paired pilot makes 80 new generation calls under a common scorer. Qwen's score gain remains 50-75 percentage points under conservative incomplete-answer bounds; Gemma's -5 to +25 interval remains inconclusive. A further 160-call crossed diagnostic finds an instruction-by-placeholder interaction, not a uniform free-form benefit. Source overlap, assistant adjudication and unresolved external impact constrain generalization.
1. Research question and contribution

A benchmark name does not uniquely identify the evaluation actually performed. The source record, its rendering, the delivered request, the parsed response and the scoring reference jointly define the measurement. Existing reproducibility guidance already documents sensitivity to prompts, metrics and implementation details [1,2]. The question here is narrower: can a concrete source-to-request or source-to-reference transformation violate an explicit task invariant, and can an intervention isolate a measurable consequence?

The contribution is an attributable case study with executable checks. It combines natural source-contract faults, prospective configuration predictions, shared-cause interventions, a paired real-model consequence analysis and explicit controls. The checker is also subjected to audit. The empirical contribution concerns these pinned failures, their consequences and the measured boundary of an implemented intervention, within established evaluation-engineering methods.
A minimal evaluation contract

Represent the official task by its kind k, question q, optional context, ordered choices O where applicable and reference semantics G. A transformation produces an effective request W and scoring reference r. The audit checks preservation of task kind, question and declared-context dependence, intended choices, official answer semantics and agreement with the actual request. Free-form G can contain accepted answer texts. Likelihood requests can be context/continuation bundles. Each protocol therefore needs an appropriate source-to-request representation.

title: Study design and natural contract failures

blocks.text: 2. Evidence stages and units

One-Eval is pinned to revision 8aba20ad17ee2c7d2391162ac03ffaebcbb17506 with open-dataflow 1.0.10. Native methods are retained under the documented import scaffolds; official records and effective request texts are captured with hashes. The stages below have different evidential roles and overlapping source questions. Their row counts must not be summed into a number of independent observations. Shared-cause and task-kind studies are detailed in Sections 7-8.
Natural mechanisms

In WinoGrande validation, the question does not affect any of 1,267 delivered prompts, and 628 references differ from source-aligned labels. The audit identifies 300 prompt groups with conflicting official labels. For a deterministic predictor using only the visible prompt, at least 309 errors are unavoidable on this fixed corpus. This is a finite-corpus information-loss statement, not a bound on arbitrary stochastic realized outputs or a new theorem.

The known-fault calibration also records 884 missing required-context dependencies among 1,000 SciQ records, plus three changed and three invalid references. In the captured LAB-Bench configuration, the official correct option is absent in all 33 records. These cases were known during checker development and are reported as calibration evidence.

The full-split counts combine these 400 with a disjoint follow-up of 27,346 captured records. They describe these source snapshots, not prevalence across arbitrary tasks, installations or users.
An audit-adapter error retained in the record

Two initial MMLU-Pro alerts were caused by native removal of option-edge whitespace. A post-outcome adapter correction was allowed only when the complete option sequence and order were preserved under str.strip(). The checker itself remained byte-identical. The follow-up found another 169 such literal-comparison alerts. All 171 are audit-adapter issues, retained separately from upstream task faults. Initial and reviewed results remain available.
3. Paired WinoGrande intervention

The frozen diagnostic panel contains 15 pairs of opposite-gold questions sharing the same native visible prompt and 20 singleton controls, yielding 50 questions in 35 dependency groups. All source questions sharing native text with the earlier pilot were excluded. Each item was evaluated under native and corrected prompts for gemma-4-31b-it and qwen3.8-27b, with option order and inference settings held fixed. The repair restores the question and removes unresolved formatting braces jointly. Its two text changes are not separately identified by this design.

The existing capture contains 200 unique requests, one attempt each: 194 completed and six incomplete. Independent request-body, terminal-response and stream-hash verification passed. The primary rule requires a completed response with one legal answer tag. Unknown responses stay in the denominator. The sensitivity interval below gives each unknown correctness in [0,1]; it is not a confidence interval.

Under unknown-as-zero, gains are +82 points for Gemma and +42 for Qwen. The conservative gain remains positive for Qwen. For Gemma, changing the ability to produce an evaluable answer contributes substantially to the observed difference, and the sensitivity interval includes zero. The archived primary analysis also reports group bootstrap intervals conditional on the scoring convention, resampling within the two diagnostic strata. Neither panel averages nor intervals estimate population prevalence.
4. Reference-only effects on the same outputs

The table below uses the pinned native heuristic parser and all captured output text, including partial text. It is a separate finite-output scoring analysis. It must not be substituted for the strict completed-answer measure above.

On identical repaired-prompt outputs, source-aligned references increase assigned scores by 42 points for Gemma and 40 for Qwen. The constant-B diagnostic scores 100% with shipped references and 50% with source references. The post-hoc prompt/reference interaction is +30 points for Gemma and -6 for Qwen. Both algebraic paths to the joint score change were verified. This decomposition describes the captured outputs; it does not establish independent effects of individual formatting operations or a change in model capability.

Usage reconciliation counts every request once, including incomplete responses: 14,547 input tokens and 97,047 output tokens. Provider-reported cost fields are preserved as units with unknown currency; project-wide spending and remaining credits are not inferred from this bounded trial.

title: Pre-inference checks and their trust boundary

blocks.text: 5. Checker calibration and controlled diagnostics

The original checker takes explicitly normalized records with actual prompt text, displayed choices, official answer semantics, parsed references and measured question/context probes. It rejects failures and incomplete evidence before calling a supplied generation function. Calibration rejected seven known faulty configurations and accepted one native One-Eval control, seven source-corrected configurations and six original EvalScope controls. Because these cases informed development, they are not independent validation.

A separate diagnostic study used 200 previously observed MMLU/MMLU-Pro source units with 11 conditions each, producing 2,200 controlled variants. The original checker accepted 800 variants involving distractor replacement/removal, duplicate gold text or partial questions. A separate source-bound wrapper added full-question substring and normalized option-multiset checks. It rejected those 800 while accepting 600 benign identity, trimming and coherent-permutation controls; it also rejected the 600 altered cases already caught by the original checks and marked 200 missing-source cases incomplete.

These are intentionally constructed development cases. The wrapper was designed after structural inspection and frozen before execution; its synthetic success is not an independent generalization estimate. A development replay on the 27,346 previously observed natural rows preserved all four panel decisions. The original checker and all first-pass false alerts remain unchanged.
6. Healthy controls in another request protocol

LM Evaluation Harness is pinned to revision d6de81643928d653435c431bae19945d41d32520. Exact native methods ran under the documented AST scaffold. A frozen rule selected 100 ARC-Challenge and 100 OpenBookQA records from already captured corpora.

All 200 cases preserve question, option order and gold index, producing 801 per-option likelihood objects. Another 200 spacing controls pass. The audit checks the context/continuation bundle through which options are delivered.

The 600 constructed carriers remove or replace a continuation, or omit the question, while retaining old metadata. The actual-request check rejects all 600. The instrumented local driver invokes its counting function for 400 accepted cases and zero rejected cases. The earlier decision-only pass and instrumentation correction are retained.

An installed-package check then used native ConfigurableTask, local loading, build_all_requests and process_results. The same 200 records produce matching 801 requests and expected outcomes for 400 constructed likelihood fixtures. Six native module hashes match the pinned checkout. A later installed source/request gate tests 1,600 conditions over these reused records. It passes 400 preserved controls, rejects 1,000 constructed alterations and blocks 200 missing-source cases. Only the 400 accepted snapshots reach the local counting sink unchanged. This measured boundary ends before model, tokenizer or remote transport execution.

title: Shared causes and a new contract prediction

blocks.text: 7. Shared input-construction causes

A fixed post-discovery diagnosis uses 633 previously captured records across seven panels and six conditions, giving 3,798 condition records. The original preprocessing, prompt resolver and locked generator/formatter method bodies run with a local recording sink. Isolated changes bind source symbols, decode parallel option lists or complete the LAB-Bench answer set.

blocks.text: The generator supplies canonical question and context variables. Templates can instead name source fields such as sentence, question_stem or support. Binding these symbols restores their dependencies. Separately, the dictionary normalizer serializes parallel label/text lists as two aggregate choices. A structure-specific decoder restores individual options. LAB-Bench demonstrates the limit of these shared fixes because its source mapping omits ideal from the option set.
A prospectively recorded MMMLU prediction

Before source-row acquisition, the fixed binding hypothesis predicted loss of the capitalized Question field in the default MMMLU FR_FR contract. From the pinned official 14,042-row CSV, 100 records were selected by canonical-JSON SHA256 order. Native question dependence is 0/100 and rises to 100/100 after the fixed binding intervention. Ordered options and the official correct option remain preserved in all 100 cases. Direct source/capture reconciliation confirms each exact prompt substitution.

This is transfer of a known mechanism to a new native configuration. MMMLU translates MMLU, so semantic questions may overlap earlier English data. The complete global exposure census remains open. These recordings use the data-only AST scaffold and local sink.

title: Task-kind loss despite internally consistent metadata

blocks.text: 8. MixEval at a heterogeneous split boundary

The gallery selects MixEval/free_form but configures a multiple-choice route and choice-letter parser. Its contract is explicitly marked inferred with smoke_passed=false. A fixed protocol precedes acquisition of the official two 2,000-row splits. Stable SHA256 order selects 100 free-form and 100 choice records. Six conditions produce 600 records. The official custom-evaluation guide distinguishes their prompt and reference semantics [10].

All 100 selected free-form rows contain the configured prompt/options/target fields, including the source placeholder options=["None"]. The wrong native route displays this placeholder as A. None and requests a choice letter; preprocessing did not create its value. Restoring question binding preserves the task-kind error. The typed generation intervention restores free-text requests in all 100 cases. Field presence and agreement among inferred settings do not detect this source-task mismatch.
Repair scope and counterexamples

The initial typed intervention changes generation while retaining incompatible scoring metadata. Section 9 separately tests reference semantics and scoring. Request-level repair alone is insufficient; the optional official rule mode also has limitations and differs from default model judging.

The initial audit expected the guide's example label single-choice, whereas the actual choice rows use multiple-choice. This causes 100 initial source-row type alerts, appearing in 300 conditions. A separate post-outcome review accepts both labels when options and integer targets are valid. All 100 rows pass that reviewed rule. One of these rows also has option-edge whitespace. Exact preservation is 99/100 and order-preserving strip-normalized preservation is 100/100. The two alert sets overlap. Initial captures and metrics remain preserved.

Choice bind_and_type repeats bind_only by design. Source records, conditions and alert appearances are reported separately. MixEval is a benchmark mixture with possible semantic overlap with earlier project data. Verification reconciles frozen selection, source hashes and request captures. The scope is native method replay through the local sink.
9. Reference exclusion can masquerade as a score

A fixed post-discovery protocol reuses 200 selected MixEval records. Four constructed-output families and three scoring conditions yield 2,400 condition records. Each case receives identical response bytes across conditions, isolating reference/parser effects from question binding or generation. The native choice rescorer rejects all 100 original list-valued references in each split and reports zero with no eligible references. This is non-evaluable, not measured zero model accuracy.

Singleton extraction is insufficient. Two five-option cases have source index 4 and correct letter E. Static A-D parsing rejects E and a one-based fallback maps index 4 to D. The typed rule dispatcher uses the original zero-based integer and all source options. Independent agent/code reconciliation verifies all 2,400 records and the frozen implementation. An integration adapter separately matches 800 official-rule controls and returns INCOMPLETE on 19 invalid-input cases.
Existing public responses, incomplete matching

A separate protocol matches the same fixed 200-source cohort to preexisting public response files. Only 49 matches are unique; 128 are unmatched and 23 ambiguous. These sets are preserved, without substitution. This is fixed-output replay, not generation under the faulty prompts or evidence that the public producer used One-Eval.

An ordinary import of the original primary metric reproduces zero with all 49 references excluded. Although its requested policy is total, the code excludes invalid references before incrementing the effective denominator. Nominal N, policy and scored N must therefore be distinguished. Conditional native accuracy is undefined. The default model-judge score and a positive model-capability gain are not established.
Official rule behavior is retained, not assumed ideal

The official optional rule mode rejects two literal accepted aliases: Government of D.C. loses its terminal period only in the response; Tomorrow is another day is truncated at is. Empty choice outputs trigger random guesses: 25/100 in the constructed seed-42 control. Five of 32 public choice texts trigger this fallback, contributing one correct guess; treating those five as unresolved gives 19-24 correct. A separate exploratory exact-alias guard fixes the two constructed misses but changes none of the 49 real-output scores. It is not independently validated or the unmodified official mode.
10. Paired real-generation follow-up

A fixed exploratory pilot selects the first 20 free-form records from the existing stable order (16 TriviaQA, three DROP, one BBH). Both prompts bind the same question/context. Binding-only retains the wrong choice instruction; typed generation uses the official free-form constructor. Two fixed models receive 80 single-attempt requests, all scored afterward with the same unmodified optional rule evaluator. Of 80 responses, 69 complete and 11 reach the 4,096-token cap; capped cases remain unknown.

These are fixed-panel sensitivity bounds, not population confidence intervals. The instruction/format intervention, exposed sources, fixed order and heuristic scoring constrain interpretation. Retrospective masked assistant review separates final factual answers from endorsed rationale content (Appendix E): Gemma can retain correct content before a final A tag. This additional construct-specific analysis preserves the original common-rule result above.
11. Relation to existing work

Reproducibility and implementation sensitivity are established concerns [1,2]. This study follows the official source semantics through task kind, request construction and reference interpretation. The collision calculation and individual invariants provide diagnostic tools within that established methodological setting.

EvalEng [7, section 7.1] recommends semantic compatibility constraints, oracle-independent scoring verification and metamorphic or differential tests. SANE [3] automates scorer-specific recipes and separates recipe alignment, realized perturbation and relation applicability. JRH [8, abstract inspected] generates judge-reliability suites. Our empirical focus is the attributable failures, controlled consequences, shared causes and configuration predictions described here. A direct comparative implementation study remains open.
12. Supported conclusions and external evidence

The audited transformations change task kind, discard question information, corrupt references or exclude every eligible case while returning a numeric score. Shared-cause interventions and the MMMLU prediction extend the explanation across configurations. WinoGrande provides a paired generation consequence. MixEval fixed-output studies isolate measurement and reference failures, with source overlap and missing cache matches retained.

Public evidence reaches upstream demos with scores/conclusions, a LoopAI execution log and copied components. No matched executable revision/request/output trace establishes an independently affected conclusion. The inspected original 100-request paper study ends before model evaluation. Bounded searches do not establish deployment frequency.
Limitations and next scientific test

Source cohorts overlap, cache matching is incomplete and post-outcome adapter reviews remain separate. The paired pilot is small, source-exposed and fixed-order. Optional rule scores differ from default model judging. Native orchestration and installed gate claims end at their declared source, provider and dependency boundaries.

A separate crossed diagnostic isolates an instruction-by-placeholder interaction (Appendices F-G); it does not support a uniform free-form benefit. Complete installed-provider execution and affected independent external conclusions remain open.

A.1 Frozen-checker transfer to Social IQa

The source-bound checker and a new deterministic adapter were frozen in research commit 832422aeb7429ba0dd29852c148a83514e940237 before acquiring source rows or observing outcomes. Social IQa was absent from the documented checker-development panels. PIQA was excluded as a new-source candidate because it appeared in an earlier audit protocol. The review was documentary and bounded: it did not establish a complete row-level exposure census across all earlier pilots and private executors.

The official Social IQa development archive contains 1,954 records. The loader is pinned to allenai/social_i_qa revision 8835ceb9141d7896d9d968634a9b21ae440e3ec5, and the archive checksum was verified. Each row was joined to its same-index one-based answer label. The first 100 records in stable SHA-256 order of canonical record/label JSON were selected without substitution. They contain 100 distinct context/question pairs and 100 distinct exact contexts; textual distinction alone does not establish statistical independence.

The custom adapter renders context and question with the three source answers and an aligned reference. Question and required-context dependence are measured with nonce substitutions. The v2 wrapper accepted all 200 preserved/permutation controls, rejected all 300 constructed-fault variants, and marked all 100 missing-source cases incomplete. The v1 checker accepted the 100 gold-preserving distractor removals. Local counting functions were invoked 400 times under v1 and 200 under v2, with no invocation after a failed or incomplete gate. These are not model requests.

Independent source-selection, answer-mapping, variant and gate reconciliation passed for all 600 variants, with no acquisition or execution errors. The original source and wrapper byte hashes are unchanged. The protocol, input records, raw labels, captures, scripts and source-revision receipts remain in the transfer archive [9].
Interpretation

This transfers already known mechanisms to a source family held out from documented checker development. The conditions are deliberately constructed using a custom adapter; they do not reveal a natural defect in a new evaluator, estimate real-world fault frequency, or validate unseen failure mechanisms. No model endpoint or native evaluator was executed. The result strengthens a bounded intervention claim while preserving the distinction between source-family transfer and globally blind validation.

title: Appendix B. Bounded native orchestration integration

blocks.text: B.1. What executes unchanged

The integration fixes code and inputs before the two task-family runs in commit 0e2616f099b5f5defb395f3d545b3736c23b063a. It reuses the same 17 free-form and 32 choice responses. Full original source modules are imported through Python package modules rather than extracting native method ASTs. One-Eval run_eval, the generator and evaluator run entry points, and FileStorage execute unchanged. This is an orchestration transfer test with replayed responses, not new model inference.

rows: Local captured-output serving; one batch per family; source-bound user-prompt and response association checked. Native default system instruction retained.
Source-bound official constructor validates question, context and ordered choices.
Per-task scoring delegates to pinned official optional rule functions; native choice post-rescoring is bypassed.
Package export facades and inert optional import sentinels avoid unrelated tensor/backend dependencies.
Source/output identity, record and response bytes, reference semantics and complete scored coverage are required before a numeric aggregate.

blocks.text: B.2. Observed scope and controls

The 17-row free-form run and 32-row choice run preserve all rows and reproduce 13 and 20 correct rule outcomes, respectively. The five choice fallback guesses remain explicit. No optional-dependency sentinel is invoked. Ten separately fixed malformed identity/coverage controls return INCOMPLETE and no aggregate before any local generation batch. The selected rows overlap the earlier fixed-output replay and are not a new independent cohort.

Native statistics retain legacy metric-name labels because the surrounding evaluator run method is unchanged. Actual scoring is explicitly identified as optional official rule mode. Native returns are diagnostic, with display_as_primary=false; the original One-Eval primary metric runner is not executed in this integration.
B.3. Provenance correction and limits

Independent review identified a metadata collision in raw score captures: an adapter field labelled source_sha256 names the scoring-code hash and overwrites the intended record-hash label during dictionary assembly. Raw results are retained. The provenance erratum separates source_record_sha256 from scorer_source_sha256 using frozen inputs and source/output association checks. Scoring outcomes and the underlying source guards are unaffected. The corrected ledger is a derived reconciliation, not a rerun.

The import facades, local provider boundary and replaced scoring methods are part of the implemented test boundary. Successful orchestration does not establish a complete installed distribution, real model transport, default judge equivalence or an externally affected conclusion.

title: Appendix C. Paired generation and capture audit

blocks.text: C.1. Fixed protocol and sources

Execution repository ricardofitas/swarm-adaption-hackathon fixes protocol af6a19b7a39643cc57d6dcf4fb1e7e9a1be319b6 and common scoring/analysis 38f2b3d556e0d5376cf14dfcb7e2b10db7f85075 before single launch 676f3b618948253a9ff4f01f400e8ab1a2971a13. Run 43606982014, attempt 1, produces 80 unique request/response records. No output-dependent source/model substitution or retry occurs. The input cohort is previously observed; these are new model responses, not new independent question families.
C.2. Pairing and unknown-answer policy

Every source/model pair receives both prompt conditions. The question and source context remain bound in both. The intervention changes the wrong choice-family instruction and official prompt wording together. A common official optional rule scorer evaluates completed nonempty outputs. Each incomplete answer remains in [0,1]; lower gain sums typed_min minus binding_max, and upper gain sums typed_max minus binding_min, over all 20 questions per model.

Among fully observed pairs, typed scoring wins on three of 14 Gemma pairs and ten of 15 Qwen pairs, with no binding-only wins. These complete-pair counts do not replace the prespecified all-20 sensitivity bounds. The same 20 source questions repeat across two models and are not 40 independent questions.
C.3. Resource and terminal-event verification

Independent reconciliation checks all 80 intent/record/artifact IDs, exact request/output/journal hashes, returned model identities, source pairing, output caps and request-start cadence. Available usage totals are 8,062 input and 66,304 output tokens. The provider cost field sums to 0.057821010000000003215 units; currency is unverified. The catalogue preflight confirms the two fixed model IDs before any generation call.

All 11 unknown answers have response.status=incomplete and reason=max_output_tokens at 4,096 tokens. Terminal SSE event type is response.completed even for these incomplete response objects. Capture completeness therefore uses the response status and full terminal/transport record, preserving all 11 as unknown. No extra judge calls are made.
C.4. Interpretation

This pilot demonstrates a model-dependent consequence of task-format repair under a common explicit scorer. It does not isolate each changed wording token, establish default judge equivalence, estimate a benchmark population gain or demonstrate an externally affected published conclusion. Raw response texts and heuristic-rule limitations remain available for audit.

The exploratory lexical review finds 14 of 18 completed Qwen binding-only texts contain only the A answer tag. A later masked assistant adjudication under fixed criteria separates final factual answers, endorsed content and common-rule credit (Appendix E). It reuses these outputs, leaves the original rule analysis unchanged and is not human or default-judge validation.
Eighteen claims retain exact evidence. C1-C16 are mapped below; C17-C18 appear in Appendices F-G. Reused sources and new responses remain separate units.

Run verify_claims.py to reconcile eighteen claims with the bundled source snapshots and hashes. Original study archives retain selection, request captures and runtime verification. Synthesis checks add no observations.

title: Appendix E. Final answers and factual content

blocks.text: E.1. Fixed retrospective review criteria

Protocol de205ec97d15cb290815063d4f190279e7410632 fixes the rubric before individual adjudication. Two assistant reviewers independently inspect all 69 complete outputs in opaque-ID order with model, condition and original score hidden. They receive the source question/context and accepted aliases. Prior aggregate exposure and possible format leakage remain; this is retrospective assistant annotation, not human annotation or the official default model judge. All 11 incomplete captures remain unknown.

The final-answer axis requires an endorsed factual answer; a bare A/None tag does not answer a source free-form task. The content axis separately credits an explicitly endorsed correct fact anywhere in the output. Incidental or negated alias mentions do not qualify. Each axis has correct, incorrect or uncertain labels. Consensus requires agreement; one disagreement about using perique as blending tobacco, without explicitly stating smoking, stays unknown.
E.2. What the disagreement between constructs shows

Reviewers agree on 68/69 labels on each axis. Seventeen completed outputs endorse the source-correct fact but end with an uninformative choice tag: 15 Gemma and two Qwen binding-only outputs. Nine of these Gemma outputs receive common-rule credit from the preceding rationale. Those are differences between whole-text credit and the declared final-answer criterion, not nine demonstrated factual false positives. One Qwen final answer, Prepare for the worst., is semantically correct despite failing the longer accepted alias But prepare for the worst.

For Gemma, binding-only has two consensus-correct final answers but 17 correct-content outputs; typed generation has 12 on both axes. Typed Gemma has five unknown labels: four incomplete captures plus the adjudication uncertainty. Qwen has two binding-only final answers and four correct-content outputs; typed generation has 15 on both axes. Original rule outcomes remain unchanged.
E.3. Bounds, verification and the next test

All bounds pair the same 20 questions per model, assigning each unknown correctness in [0,1]. They are finite-panel sensitivity bounds, not confidence intervals. Source/request identities, packet/key bijection, grounded excerpts and independent aggregate reconstruction pass. No new model or judge API calls are made. The review does not establish hidden capability loss or population superiority; the resulting instruction-by-carrier diagnostic on a disjoint question panel is reported in Appendices F-G. The source pool was previously audited.

title: Appendix F. Crossed instruction and carrier

blocks.text: F.1. Fixed design and authenticated execution (C17)

Twenty source questions are crossed with two models, free-form versus choice instructions, and an appended A.None carrier present versus absent. Source question/context and answer-tag requirements are fixed within each source. The absent condition removes only the appended carrier; one BBH source retains its intrinsic Yes/No options. Questions are exact-text disjoint from the previous generation panel but drawn from a previously audited pool. This is a custom diagnostic, not a native official benchmark run or globally blind transfer.

Protocol/implementation ddedfcd6 and launch 3faed45d precede all responses. Run 43615821403, attempt 1, records 160 unique attempts: 152 complete and 8 incomplete. All 160 terminal events are named response.completed, but the eight incomplete response statuses remain unknown. The pre-inspection independent verifier (4981202b) matches exact Git bytes and passes source/request/output/journal/model/ledger/usage/cap checks and independent enumeration of all five contrasts.
Every condition retains 20 planned source questions per model. Correct counts are the frozen optional official RULE assignments, not semantic adjudication or default model-judge scores.

rows: Interaction: instruction gain absent minus present

blocks.text: Carrier removal improves assigned score under choice instructions, but not consistently under free-form instructions. The negative interaction is supported under every assignment of missing outcomes within this fixed panel; a generic free-form-instruction advantage is not. These deterministic sensitivity bounds use 20 paired questions per model, not 160 independent questions or population confidence intervals.

No retry or resume. Usage: 27,768 input and 79,481 output tokens; reported cost 0.094558622000000007143 units, currency unverified. Per-request output cap 4,096; eight incomplete captures remain unknown. No new calls were made during result collection or adjudication.
G.1. Prespecified masked review and distinct endpoints (C18)

The secondary rubric was frozen before factorial responses existed. Two assistant reviewers inspect all 152 eligible texts in SHA256opaque-ID order, with model, instruction, carrier, request and primary score hidden. They receive the frozen source question/context and accepted answers. The final-answer axis requires the factual final commitment; endorsed content can occur anywhere. Correct labels require verbatim evidence. A third agent independently verifies identities, quotes, consensus arithmetic and all five contrasts without importing the production analyzers.

Reviewers agree 152/152 on each axis and tag format. All 152 complete responses have compliant answer tags, which does not establish factual correctness. Eight incomplete captures remain unknown. Two additional complete Gemma responses ask for clarification on the undated Defence Secretary question and stay uncertain. Multipart age ranges and source-intrinsic Yes/No options were explicitly identified before generation; the rubric requires all requested parts without mutating original RULE scoring.
G.2. Communication failure and rule credit are distinguishable

For Gemma under choice plus A.None, the primary rule credits 8/20; the assistant final-answer axis accepts 1/20, while endorsed content accepts 16/20. Fifteen outputs contain the required fact but commit to a non-informative final answer; seven of those receive RULE credit. This distinguishes whole-text credit, final communication and visible factual content. Those seven are not demonstrated factual false positives. For Qwen in the same condition, neither final nor content is accepted among 18 complete responses, with 2 incomplete remaining unknown.
G.3. Scientific boundary

The primary endpoint remains unchanged. These are same-family assistant judgments, not human gold labels or the default MixEval judge; agreement does not imply statistically independent errors. Source gold is not independently fact-checked, and output style can reveal condition. The fixed panel is exposed, custom wording is used and counterbalancing is deterministic. The interaction identifies a conditional response-and-measurement mechanism for these tested transformations, not universal capability loss, hidden knowledge or external deployment impact.
